Here's the latest
• Historic talks: The first ever joint US-China-Russia leaders’ meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin has concluded, according to Chinese state TV. Trump said he was charting a “different course” in foreign policy by meeting jointly, and echoed Xi’s emphasis on the leaders’ joint responsibility to engage.
• Trump touts friendship: The US president earlier met with both leaders separately, telling Xi their “outstanding personal relationship” serves people in both the US and China “very well” and describing Putin as “my friend.”
• Trump talks tech: Trump offered a cautiously positive outlook on AI in an earlier speech to Asian leaders in China, saying the new tech required care. In an interview with Fox News, Trump urged Americans concerned about a recent spate of tech outages back home to “relax,” saying the incidents were “individual events.”

In photos: Unprecedented trilateral talks between US, Russia and China
By CNN staff
US President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin just held historic three-way talks in Shenzhen, southern China, against the backdrop of the APEC summit.
The meeting lasted for about an hour and a half, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.
Trump said he was charting a “different course” in US foreign policy.
“As presidents of three of the world’s largest countries, we have a special responsibility to maintain open, respectful and productive dialogue on issues impacting not just our people, but the entire planet,” he said at the start of the historic talks. “Too often past leaders avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements, and we feel the opposite, and we think that we are sure about that.”
China's President Xi Jinping (center) US President Donald Trump (right) and Russia's President Vladimir Putin (left) hold a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday.

Trump, Putin and Xi just got out of talks. Here's what else happened in China today
By Lauren Kent
Various
Donald Trump just joined historic trilateral talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, which the US president said showed that his administration was charting a “different course” in foreign policy.
The meeting only lasted about an hour and a half – but is an optics win for both Russia and China.
Xi, who hosted the meeting, suggested China, Russia, and the US should maintain regular high-level exchanges. But we don’t yet know what leaders talked about while they were in the room.
Here’s what else to know about today’s events in China:
Trump touts 'outstanding personal relationship' with Xi
0:45
Trump touts 'outstanding personal relationship' with Xi
0:45
One-on-one with Putin: Trump also met Putin for about 40 minutes on Thursday, describing the Russian strongman as “my friend” before their sit-down. The White House described it as a “pull-aside” – a less formal designation than a bilateral meeting. Trump walked into the room flanked by his Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
By Austin Mabeus, CNN

'He’s my friend': Trump praises Putin as their meeting gets underway
President Donald Trump praised Russian leader Vladimir Putin as the two sat down for a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit Thursday.
'He’s my friend': Trump praises Putin as their meeting gets underway
0:43
Iran war comment: In an interview with Fox News from China, Trump dismissed the notion that he would seek help from Russia and China in ending the war with Iran during the leaders’ trilateral meeting. “You know, we don’t need any help… they want to make a deal, so I don’t need help,” Trump said.
Nvidia scandal: The resignation of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid national security concerns has loomed over Trump’s visit to China. On Thursday, a Bloomberg reporter was banned from the trilateral meeting after she called out a question about Huang.
Nuclear weapons: Trump teased the prospect of discussing denuclearization in his meetings at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Trump said that countries “only need about 10” nuclear weapons, but acknowledged the difficulty in persuading other countries to give up their stockpiles.
CNN’s Jessie Yeung, Lex Harvey, Kevin Liptak, Kristen Holmes, Sylvie Zhuang and Aleena Fayaz contributed to this post.
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 4:57 AM ET
Published Nov 19, 2026, 4:57 AM ET
Trump-Xi-Putin meeting ends after an hour and a half, Chinese state media reports
By Jessie Yeung
The trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russia’s Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping has ended, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV. It lasted roughly an hour and a half.
The leaders delivered opening remarks before the talks, saying they would discuss nuclear disarmament and the Russia-Ukraine war, among other topics.
All emphasized the need for engagement between the three foremost nuclear-armed nations.
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 4:52 AM ET
Published Nov 19, 2026, 4:52 AM ET
Three-way talks are still ongoing, more than an hour in
By Jessie Yeung and Sylvie Zhuang
Trump, Xi Jinping and Putin attend a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on Thursday.
Win McNamee/Getty Images
The trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russia’s Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping is still ongoing more than an hour after it began, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.
Evening is falling, with footage showing the leaders’ staff and motorcades waiting outside the venue at Kylin Villa, a resort in China’s tech hub Shenzhen, against a darkening sky.
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 4:44 AM ET
Published Nov 19, 2026, 4:44 AM ET
Xi proposed four points for major powers to get along
By Sylvie Zhuang
China's President Xi Jinping takes part in a trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump and Russia's President Vladimir Putin at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen.
Andres Martinez Casares/AFP/Pool/Getty Images
Hosting the trilateral meeting, President Xi Jinping put forward a four-point proposal for major powers to get along, according to state media CCTV.
Xi said major powers need to uphold mutual respect; peaceful coexistence; cooperation for mutual benefit; and finally, maintain dialogue and communications.
Xi warned that “without communication, suspicion will spread, and minor frictions could escalate into major conflicts.”
China and the US have in recent years clashed over the fate of the self-ruled island of Taiwan. China has repeatedly warned the US that Taiwan is a “red line” issue in the bilateral relationship that the US should not cross.
Xi further suggested China, Russia, and the US should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep channels of dialogue open at all levels, and establish mechanisms for crisis communication to avoid miscalculations.
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 4:35 AM ET
Published Nov 19, 2026, 4:35 AM ET
Trump said he would discuss "rogue globalist organizations" with Xi and Putin
By Kevin Liptak in Shenzhen, China
Among the areas of discussion President Donald Trump previewed in his opening remarks at the trilateral meeting Thursday was ways to “protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations.”
He cited specifically the International Criminal Court as an institution “which has gotten out of control” and “strayed far beyond its jurisdiction.”
The Trump administration has waged a campaign against the ICC, including sanctions and travel restrictions against some of its officials.
The court has issued an arrest warrant for Russian President Vladimir Putin over alleged war crimes.
Part of Trump’s animus toward the court stems from its association with Jack Smith, who worked there as a prosecutor before serving as special counsel investigating Trump.
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 4:34 AM ET
Published Nov 19, 2026, 4:34 AM ET
Reporter banned from trilateral after asking question about Jensen Huang
By Lex Harvey
A Bloomberg reporter was banned from the trilateral meeting by China after she called out a question about the former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during President Donald Trump’s meeting earlier with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, according to a report shared with journalists.
The question was: “President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?”
The White House advocated for the reporter’s inclusion but Chinese officials refused to budge, according to the report.
The Chinese government told reporters that yelling questions is considered extremely rude.
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 3:51 AM ET
Published Nov 19, 2026, 3:51 AM ET
Trump says historic talks with US adversaries are charting a "different course"
By Kevin Liptak in Shenzhen, China
Host TV
President Donald Trump said he was charting a “different course” in foreign policy by meeting jointly for the first time with his Russian and Chinese counterparts.
Referring warmly to Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin — whom Trump referred to by his first name — Trump said he believed engaging US adversaries could yield results.
“As presidents of three of the world’s largest countries, we have a special responsibility to maintain open, respectful and productive dialogue on issues impacting not just our people, but the entire planet,” he said at the start of the historic talks.
“Too often past leaders avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements, and we feel the opposite, and we think that we are sure about that.”
Trump said that “no problems were ever solved” by refusing to talk with leaders where there are disagreements.
“So, no peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech together,” he said. “We are choosing a different course.”
He said nuclear disarmament would be up for discussion in the summit, although he acknowledged that convincing a country to rid itself of weapons would be hard.
“Once you have the nuclear weapons, it’s very hard to not have them,” he said. “It’s the way life works.”
And he voiced optimism that a resolution to the war in Ukraine could be near.
“I think things are happening. I think that (Putin) and I hope the other side would like to see an end to that war,” he said.
While expectations have been low for major breakthroughs from today’s meeting, Trump said it was possible.
“Let’s see if we can get something done,” he said before the press was dismissed and the meeting got underway.
